Future Present Labs
Inference substrate

One resident model.
Modular behavior.

UMIE — Universal Modular Inference Engine — is FPL’s Rust inference substrate. It keeps a base model resident while loading validated behavior assets around it.

Built for the fungOS ecosystem, with Apple Silicon and NVIDIA backends behind explicit execution contracts.

Load behavior, keep the base

Assets
Adapters, constrained decision plans, fusers and quantization recipes have validated identities.
Decisions
RLCD scores bounded, schema-constrained choices directly from model logits.
Model specs
Instruction-bounded Lua resolves model-specific tensor mappings into a backend-neutral Rust plan.
Residency
Rust owns tensor bytes, memory, scheduling and execution. Cache identities include the inputs that change tensor or KV semantics.

Explicit interfaces

The SDK documents Rust and C ABI integration. The serving layer exposes model discovery, health and monitoring endpoints alongside the System One contract.

GET /health
GET /v1/models
GET /metrics

Model families and execution features depend on the selected backend and validated model specification.

Project status

Active development. Autoregressive text, diffusion-transformer images and constrained decisions are execution targets; backend and model coverage varies. A readable checkpoint is accepted for execution only when its required operators and native encodings are supported.
